title: Solovay's theorem: ZF+DC consistent with all reals Lebesgue measurable

problemStatement.formal: Con(ZFC + \exists \text{ inaccessible cardinal}) \Rightarrow Con(ZF + DC + \forall A \subseteq \mathbb{R},\ A \text{ is Lebesgue measurable})
problemStatement.plain: The Axiom of Choice is what lets one build non-measurable sets of reals (Vitali sets) and paradoxes like Banach-Tarski. Solovay (1970) proved that if one keeps only Dependent Choice (DC), it is consistent that EVERY subset of the reals is Lebesgue measurable, so such pathologies are artifacts of full AC rather than facts of mathematics. Meanwhile the uncountability of the reals (#R = c), formalized in the parent entry, needs no AC and survives untouched. The theorem is proved by forcing (the Levy collapse of an inaccessible cardinal, then passing to L(R)).
whyMatters: Draws the precise line between AC-free real analysis (uncountability of R, transcendentals, Borel measure theory) and AC-dependent pathology (Vitali sets, Banach-Tarski, well-ordering R)
Complements the parent uncountability proof: shows that adding 'every set is measurable' does not collapse #R = c, answering which uncountability phenomena require AC
A landmark forcing result whose inaccessible-cardinal hypothesis is necessary (Shelah 1984), and a grand-challenge stress test for set-theoretic formalization in Lean/Mathlib

proven: Solovay's theorem (Solovay 1970, Annals of Math 92:1-56) via the Levy collapse of an inaccessible cardinal
Necessity of the inaccessible for 'all sets measurable' (Shelah 1984)
AC implies a non-measurable (Vitali) set exists (ZFC theorem; formalized in Mathlib)
R is uncountable in plain ZF (parent entry: Cardinal.mk_real, aleph0_lt_continuum)
Borel and analytic sets are measurable in ZF+DC (Lusin)
open: No part of Solovay's argument is formalized in Lean 4 / Mathlib (no Levy collapse forcing, no L(R), no measurability transfer)
Mathlib has no general forcing framework (conditions, generic filters, forcing relation, names, truth lemma)
Mathlib has no theory of the constructible universe L or L(R) / inner models
knownResults.goal: Produce a Lean 4 formalization brief and, as far as tractable, a faithful formal STATEMENT of Solovay's relative-consistency theorem (defining inaccessible cardinal, Levy collapse, L(R), 'Lebesgue measurable') plus the ZF-only AC-isolation lemmas (Vitali needs AC; #R = c does not). A complete machine-checked proof is a moonshot gated on a Mathlib forcing framework.
